title: Hotfix: Backport host/origin validation to requests and websocket connections
body:
## What I did

This is a backport of #33835 for Storybook v9.1.

#### Manual testing

- Run `npx ngrok http 6006`
- Verify that the ngrok URL serves an Invalid host error
- Update `.storybook/main.ts` to set `core.allowedHosts` to include the ngrok hostname (no protocol), then restart Storybook

comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**`allowedHosts` may drift between first-pass config and runtime enforcement.**

`allowedHosts` is captured from the first `presets.apply('core')`, but runtime checks are driven later from final presets in `storybookDevServer`. If a later preset mutates `core.allowedHosts`, the warning/startup output here can diverge from actual behavior.

Consider re-reading `allowedHosts` from the final preset pass before emitting warnings/startup info.



Also applies to: 271-271

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/core/src/core-server/build-dev.ts` around lines 143 - 156, The warning
uses allowedHosts captured from the initial presets.apply('core', {}) call which
can differ from the final runtime presets used by storybookDevServer; update the
logic in build-dev.ts to re-fetch or read core.allowedHosts from the final
preset pass (the same presets used by storybookDevServer) immediately before the
host === '0.0.0.0' check so the message reflects runtime enforcement, i.e.,
replace or refresh the earlier allowedHosts value obtained from
presets.apply('core', {}) with the final preset result before emitting the
logger.warn that references allowedHosts.
```

</details>

<!-- fingerprinting:phantom:medusa:hawk -->

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment by CodeRabbit -->
comments.label_reasoning: The allowedHosts value used for warnings may diverge from the value actually enforced at runtime, meaning the displayed behavior does not match actual behavior.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests re-reading allowedHosts from the final preset pass before emitting warnings to avoid divergence between config and runtime enforcement.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Update stale `allowedHosts` documentation text.**

Line 48 says host validation is “currently only for WebSocket connections”, but this PR also introduces HTTP Host-header validation middleware. Please align the comment with actual behavior.



<details>
<summary>📝 Suggested doc fix</summary>

```diff
-   * Enable hostname validation, currently only for WebSocket connections. Set to `[]` to disallow
-   * all hosts except known local/network address, or `true` to allow all hosts.
+   * Enable hostname validation for development HTTP requests and WebSocket connections.
+   * Set to `[]` to disallow all hosts except known local/network addresses, or `true` to allow all hosts.
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/core/src/types/modules/core-common.ts` around lines 47 - 50, The comment
for the allowedHosts option is stale: update the documentation for the
allowedHosts property (in core-common.ts) to state that hostname validation
applies to both WebSocket connections and HTTP Host-header validation
middleware, and clarify semantics for values (e.g., `[]` to disallow all
non-local hosts, `true` to allow all hosts, or a list of allowed hostnames) so
the doc matches the implemented behavior.
```

</details>
